issue.title: Provide raw headers when using akka-http backend

repository.name: playframework
repository.description: The Community Maintained High Velocity Web Framework For Java and Scala.

issue.body:
Hello,

I just ran into an issue with Akka HTTP parsing an Authorization header in a weird way, which in my case ended up in experiencing errors because I'm doing authentication delegation by forwarding the header to another service which did not expect this "format".

Akka HTTP seems to provide `RawHeader` instances according to the documentation (http://doc.akka.io/docs/akka-http/10.0.9/scala/http/common/http-model.html#http-headers). It would be nice to have access to those from the Play API for such cases. I'm not sure what would make more sense API-wise though. For now, I'm going to use Netty.

### Play Version (2.5.x / etc)
2.6.3

### API (Scala / Java / Neither / Both)
Scala

body: Hey, are there any news on this? We would really like to migrate to Play 2.6 and this blocks us from doing so right now.

@dietmax Perhaps I don't understand the problem fully, but if the problem is Play's akka-http server as we suspect, it should not be a blocker in updating. You should be able to switch to the Netty server (which is still 100% supported), or you can just use the standard APIs for getting headers, which are case insensitive (e.g. `request.headers.get(AUTHORIZATION)`).

I agree it's a good idea to preserve the case here though.

> I agree it's a good idea to preserve the case here though.

well basically it might be a good idea, but actually http headers are case-insensitive. This matters a lot on http2 where a lot of implementations do lowercase every header even on http/1.1 for forward compatibility.

@gmethvin Switching to the netty server is definitely something we will look into, thanks for that tip 👍 Regarding the standard API for getting headers, my understanding is, that `request.headers` is just a wrapper around a `Map[String, String]` and HeaderNames.AUTHORIZATION is the String "Authorization". Therefore `request.headers.get("Authorization")` will only return Uppercase authorization headers, which is the behavior that causes my problem. Or am I missing something here?

@dietmax The `Headers` class internally uses a `Map` but it is a `TreeMap` with a [case insensitive ordering](https://github.com/playframework/playframework/blob/2.6.x/framework/src/play/src/main/scala/play/api/mvc/Headers.scala#L101). Headers are case-insensitive, so the headers API is case insensitive.

Thanks to @gmethvin s comment I finally came around to the fact that `request.headers.keys.contains(HeaderNames.AUTHORIZATION)` does not behave in the same way that `request.headers.get(HeaderNames.AUTHORIZATION).isDefined` does. Transforming the `TreeMap` to a `Set` works around the logic that enables case insensitivity. That is where our error came from. Thank you!

We've also observed that when using the default Akka-Http engine in Play 2.6, the header name will be lower-cased if it's 'invalid' in some way. In particular, for two HTTP requests supplying `User-Agent` (ie capitalised), the headers map will have either `User-Agent` or `user-agent` depending on whether Akka-HTTP thinks the User-Agent string is valid:

With a valid `User-Agent`:
```
curl -H "User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 11_2_2 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/604.4.7 (KHTML, like Gecko) Mobile/15C202" localhost:9000/test

headers.toSimpleMap=Map(Host -> localhost:8970, Accept -> */*, User-Agent -> Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 11_2_2 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/604.4.7 (KHTML, like Gecko) Mobile/15C202, Content-Type -> none/none, Remote-Address -> 127.0.0.1:44698, ...)
```


With an invalid `User-Agent` (actually sent by the Facebook iOS app):
```
$ curl -H "User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 11_2_2 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/604.4.7 (KHTML, like Gecko) Mobile/15C202 [FBAN/FBIOS;FBAV/155.0.0.36.93;FBBV/87992437;FBDV/iPhone9,3;FBMD/iPhone;FBSN/iOS;FBSV/11.2.2;FBSS/2;FBCR/3Ireland;FBID/phone;FBLC/en_US;FBOP/5;FBRV/0]" localhost:9000/test

[WARN] [01/24/2018 15:21:13.122] [play-dev-mode-akka.actor.default-dispatcher-10] [akka.actor.ActorSystemImpl(play-dev-mode)] Illegal header: Illegal 'user-agent' header: Invalid input '[', expected 'EOI', product-or-comment, WSP, comment or CRLF (line 1, column 112): Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 11_2_2 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/604.4.7 (KHTML, like Gecko) Mobile/15C202 [FBAN/FBIOS;FBAV/155.0.0.36.93;FBBV/87992437;FBDV/iPhone9,3;FBMD/iPhone;FBSN/iOS;FBSV/11.2.2;FBSS/2;FBCR/3Ireland;FBID/phone;FBLC/en_US;FBOP/5;FBRV/0]

headers.toSimpleMap=Map(Host -> localhost:8970, Accept -> */*, user-agent -> Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 11_2_2 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/604.4.7 (KHTML, like Gecko) Mobile/15C202 [FBAN/FBIOS;FBAV/155.0.0.36.93;FBBV/87992437;FBDV/iPhone9,3;FBMD/iPhone;FBSN/iOS;FBSV/11.2.2;FBSS/2;FBCR/3Ireland;FBID/phone;FBLC/en_US;FBOP/5;FBRV/0], Content-Type -> none/none, Remote-Address -> 127.0.0.1:44116, ...)
```

Lower-case for invalid, capitalised for valid! Where is that documented?!
I'm working on Akka HTTP backend header issues right now. I'm going to re-open this issue so we can track it.

issue.title: Don't parse headers in Akka HTTP

repository.name: playframework
repository.description: The Community Maintained High Velocity Web Framework For Java and Scala.

issue.body:
Fixes #7733,  #7735, #7737 (maybe main issue, definitely `User-Agent` example), #7719, #7997, #8205. Also maybe fixes #8149 (unverified right now).

A recent change to Akka HTTP allows us to disable header parsing. Disabling header parsing, where possible, should fix bugs and improve performance.

This PR is ready now that Akka HTTP 10.0.13 has been released with the following patch: https://github.com/akka/akka-http/pull/1937.
